title: resume
description:
Replay buffered pushes after a reconnect (spec §10).

The caller states the last `seq` it actually received; the plugin re-sends everything newer from its ring buffer, then returns to live. The ring holds the last 1000 pushes and lives on the plugin, not on the connection — a per-connection buffer would have nothing to replay, which is the whole point.

Two failure modes the result exists to surface:

`gap: true` — the requested position had already been overwritten, so some pushes are gone for good. The caller should re-sync with `discover` plus `readState` rather than pretend it has a complete picture.

`seq` below the caller's `since_seq` — the plugin restarted and its counter went back to the beginning. The caller must clamp its expectation to this value instead of discarding every push as a duplicate, which is what it would otherwise do until the counter caught up.

sending.title: Backlog size
sending.description: How many buffered pushes follow before live traffic resumes. 0 is normal — it means the caller was already current.

seq.title: Sender position before this call
seq.description: The plugin's current counter. Present so the caller can detect a restart and clamp.

gap.title: Whether pushes were lost
gap.description: True when `since_seq` fell off the back of the ring buffer.
